transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to see me?

I came in because I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt, and I kept having these awful thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like if I put one photo in the wrong place or chose the wrong color, it meant I didn’t love her enough. They didn’t feel like normal creative doubts—I couldn’t just let them go.
When those thoughts came up, did you feel driven to do specific repetitive actions or mental routines to try to make the bad feeling go away?

Yeah. I’ll reread the label text, nudge the same objects on the table, and check photos of the layout over and over until it feels settled. Part of me knows it’s already fine, but I keep doing it and lose studio time.
Do these thoughts and repetitive habits feel like unwanted, distressing intrusions that you wish you could stop?
Yes, definitely. They feel intrusive and upsetting, not like thoughts I want to have. I know a photo placement or color choice shouldn’t mean I loved my aunt less, but I can’t just brush it off.
